text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired: prometheus_scrape_failures > 50 in last 5m for job=redwood-node-exporter on cluster=eu-west-1 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Pager triggered: PD-INC-8942 — paging primary on-call
Robert (oncall): acked the page :white_check_mark:
Robert (oncall): I'm on it. anyone seeing anything in grafana or logs?
Maya: dashboards show huge drop in node_exporter scrape success % across eu-west-1; latency on pushgateway increasing too
Ashwin: also seeing a surge of consumer lag in kafka topic metrics-log-ingest: group=log-ingest-consumer group_lag ~ 1.2M
Jess: logstore write queue growing, backpressure metric spiking: logqueue.size ~ 480k, ingestion_throughput down 70%
Tim: hypothesis: log ingester backlog is causing downstream Prometheus exporters to time out when scraping, causing scrape failures to cascade
Robert (oncall): ok, triage plan: 1) reduce scrape load (lower scrape interval / disable non-critical exporters) 2) mitigate log backlog (scale consumer / restart stuck pods) 3) assess customer impact & notify if dashboards/customers affected
Maya: I'll flip non-essential scrapes to 60s -> 120s for eu-west scrape targets. doing it via configmap patch now.
Maya:  kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prometheus-scrape-config --patch '"data":{"scrape_interval_override":"120s"}'  (applying)
Maya: update applied. scrapes should drop within one scrape cycle.
Ashwin: I'm scaling log-ingest-consumer to 10 -> 30 replicas, scaling now:  kubectl -n ingest scale deployment/log-ingest-consumers --replicas=30
infra-bot: action: scaled deployment/log-ingest-consumers to 30 replicas by Ashwin
Jess: restarting the two log-forwarder pods that had OOMKilled recently: kubectl -n ingest rollout restart deployment/log-forwarder
Jess: also bumping consumer JVM heap for this deploy to 12g (temp)
Robert (oncall): good. I'll pause the PD alarm for scrape failures while we stabilize to avoid noise. leaving a 30m suppression.
incident-bot: alert suppression in place for prometheus_scrape_failures (30m) by Robert (oncall)
Tim: running quick health check on kafka: kafka-consumer-lag-exporter shows partition hotness on brokers b2,b3; adding an extra broker client thread pool is probably helpful; triggering a rolling restart of consumer group coordinator isn't ideal during high lag though
Maya: scrape success rate recovering to ~92% after scrape interval adjust, previously 60%
Ashwin: consumer lag trending down after scale and restarts; from 1.2M -> 280k in 6m
Jess: logqueue size dropping: 480k -> 95k, ingestion throughput back to ~80% of baseline
Robert (oncall): great. customer impact: looked at support-recent incidents — two dashboards reported stale graphs (internal analytics customers). I pinged the customer success rep to notify impacted customers with an ETA (30-45m)
Maya: can we re-enable higher scrape frequency for critical exporters only? I suggest keep node_exporter at 120s for now, but set app-level exporters to 30s for prod namespaces
Tim: agreed. doing a selective patch for prod namespaces now.  kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prometheus-scrape-config --patch '...prod targets:30s...'
incident-bot: note added to incident: runbook followed: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/metrics-ingest (steps 1-5)
PagerDuty: Incident PD-INC-8942 acknowledged by Robert (oncall). Next escalation at +15m if unresolved.
Ashwin: observed an edge: one ingester pod had disk pressure evicting the sidecar exporter; increased EBS throughput for that node to reduce eviction events
Jess: rebalanced hot partitions in kafka topic metrics-log-ingest -> reassigning 6 partitions from b3 to b1,b4 (no downtime planned).
Robert (oncall): are there any automation rollback steps if scaling causes thrash?
Maya: yes, we have a rollback script: /ops/playbooks/ingest-scale-rollback.sh — it will step down replicas and revert JVM heap. I'm standing by to run if we see thrashing
Tim: verifying dashboards & alerting: synthetic queries for critical dashboards returning expected values now. will keep monitoring for 20m
Ashwin: consumer lag now ~42k, logqueue ~24k, prometheus scrape success ~98%
Robert (oncall): excellent. I'll close the PD incident once we feel stable for 30m. leaving a postmortem stub: https://incidents.redwood/PD-8942/postmortem-draft
Jess: note for postmortem: consider adding guardrails for consumer autoscaling and disk pressure alerts earlier in the pipeline
Maya: also recommend adding fallback scrape routing to secondary prometheus in non-prod to avoid single-point-of-failure for exporters
Tim: adding bullet about customer communication: CSE sent initial note to affected customers, follow-up planned after postmortem
Robert (oncall): handing off to Ashwin for follow-up monitoring and cleanup, I'll go to sleep but reachable if something flares. :zzz:
Ashwin: taking over monitoring and cleanup. will file a config PR to make temporary scrape adjustments revert automatically after 1h
incident-bot: incident PD-INC-8942 status: Stabilizing — acknowledged, suppression active, owner=Ashwin
infra-bot: created an action item: PR #4526 to revert scrape interval changes in 1h by Maya
Tim: final check: no alerts firing for the last 3m. I'll keep an eye until 2063412600
Robert (oncall): thanks team. good coordination. :clap:
Jess: two follow-ups for tomorrow: 1) upgrade kafka broker b3 disk, 2) add consumer lag alert runbook details
Ashwin: filing tickets for both now
incident-bot: thread closed for active paging; leave notes in postmortem and set reminder to review in 24h by Robert (oncall)
